facts.statement: Amazonsaurus is a genus of dinosaur.
facts.quote: genus: Amazonsaurus

facts.statement: The only known species is Amazonsaurus maranhensis.
facts.quote: species: maranhensis

facts.statement: Carvalho et al. described Amazonsaurus in 2003.
facts.quote: parent_authority: Carvalho et al., 2003

facts.statement: Amazonsaurus lived during the Early Cretaceous Period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Early Cretaceous,

facts.statement: Amazonsaurus was a large, four-legged herbivore with a long neck and a whiplash-style tail.
facts.quote: It would have been a large-bodied quadrupedal herbivore with a long neck and whiplash tail.

facts.statement: Unlike some of the longest animals ever, Amazonsaurus was likely no more than 12 meters (40 feet) long.
facts.quote: Although more derived diplodocoids were some of the longest animals ever to exist, Amazonsaurus was probably not more than 12 meters (40 ft) long.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated Amazonsaurus weighed 5000 kg in 2010.
facts.quote: Gregory S. Paul estimated in 2010 its weight at 5000 kg.

facts.statement: Amazonsaurus lived between 125 and 100 million years ago during the Aptian and Albian epochs.
facts.quote: This geologic formation dates back to the Aptian through Albian epochs of the Early Cretaceous, or about 125 to 100 million years ago.

facts.statement: Amazonsaurus lived in floodplain deposits near a river delta.
facts.quote: Amazonsaurus was recovered in sediments which are interpreted by geologists as floodplain deposits near a river delta.

facts.statement: Amazonsaurus fossils were first found in the Mata locality in the Brazilian Amazon.
facts.quote: Fossils of Amazonsaurus were first unearthed in the Mata locality in Itapecuru-Mirim County, Maranhão Province in the Brazilian Amazon.

facts.statement: This discovery was the first of dinosaur fossils in the Amazon Basin and the first record of a sauropod from the Lower Cretaceous of Brazil.
facts.quote: This was the first discovery of dinosaur fossils in the Amazon Basin and one of few known from northern Brazil and the first record of a sauropod from the Lower Cretaceous of Brazil.

facts.statement: Ismar de Souza Carvalho, Leonardo dos Santos Avilla, and Leonardo Salgado named Amazonsaurus maranhensis in 2003.
facts.quote: In 2003, Brazilian paleontologists Ismar de Souza Carvalhoa and Leonardo dos Santos Avilla and Argentine paleontologist Leonardo Salgado scientifically described the remains and assigned them to a new genus and species of sauropod, which they named Amazonsaurus maranhensis.

facts.statement: Elver Luiz Mayer estimated Amazonsaurus was around 10 meters long, while Gregory S. Paul estimated it was 12 meters long and 5000 kg.
facts.quote: Amazonsaurus was a relatively small sauropod, with Brazilian professor Elver Luiz Mayer estimating it to be around 10 m in length, while American paleontologist Gregory S. Paul placed it at 12 m long and 5000 kg in mass.

facts.statement: Unlike other rebbachisaurids, the neural spines on Amazonsaurus tail vertebrae were straight and inclined backward.
facts.quote: Unlike other rebbachisaurids, the neural spines (large extensions from the tops of vertebrae) on the caudal vertebrae are straight and posteriorly (towards the back) inclined.

facts.statement: The neural spines on Amazonsaurus tail vertebrae were oriented at a 45-degree angle from the middle of the vertebra body.
facts.quote: This spine is oriented at a 45 degree angle and is set up at around the middle of the centrum (the body of the vertebra).

facts.statement: The neural arches of Amazonsaurus tail vertebrae were extremely tall, a trait typical of diplodocoids.
facts.quote: The caudal neural arches are extremely tall, typical of diplodocoids.

facts.statement: Amazonsaurus had dorsal vertebrae with slightly opisthocoelous (convex front, concave back) centra that were wide and low.
facts.quote: Its dorsal vertebrae bear slightly opisthocoelus (convex front and concave back ends), wide, and low centra.

facts.statement: The bottom of Amazonsaurus dorsal vertebrae was flat, giving them a squared shape.
facts.quote: These centra have flat ventral (bottom) sides, creating a squared shape.

facts.statement: Deep pleurocoels, which held air sacs, occupied most of the internal space on the sides of Amazonsaurus dorsal vertebrae.
facts.quote: On the lateral (side) faces are deep pleurocoels (large fossae that bore air sacs) which take up most of the internal space of the sides of the centra.

facts.statement: Amazonsaurus chevrons were L-shaped with open haemal canals and a posterior distal process, differing from those of Limaysaurus.
facts.quote: The chevrons are distinct in their open haemal canals and relatively elongated, laterally thin shafts. They are L-shaped overall with a posterior distal process, unlike those of Limaysaurus.

facts.statement: The known pelvis of Amazonsaurus consists only of fragments from the pubis and the left ilium.
facts.quote: The pelvis is only represented by fragments from the proximal (towards body) and mid-sections of the pubis as well as the left ilium.

facts.statement: The ilium of Amazonsaurus was wide, high, and had pneumatic adaptations.
facts.quote: Overall, the ilium is transversely (left-to-right) wide, high, and bears pneumatic (air-bearing) adaptations.

facts.statement: Amazonsaurus lived in the middle of the Cretaceous Period, about 100 million years ago, in what is now South America.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 100 millones de años, en el Albiense, en lo que hoy es Sudamérica.

facts.statement: Amazonsaurus was a relatively small herbivorous sauropod with a long neck, a whiplash tail, a length of about 11 meters, a height of 4.5 meters, and a weight of only 10 tons.
facts.quote: Amazonsaurus era un saurópodo herbívoro relativamente pequeño, con un largo cuello, una cola con forma de látigo y un largo aproximado de 11 metros, un alto de 4,5 metros y solo 10 toneladas de peso.

facts.statement: Professor Cândido Simões discovered the first vertebrae of Amazonsaurus in 1991 after studying the area for 40 years.
facts.quote: Los estudios en esta área se han realizado desde hace 40 años por el profesor de la UFRJ, Cândido Simões, que en 1991 encontró la vértebras del Amazonasaurus.

facts.statement: Researchers identified the new species after finding about 100 fragments, mostly neural spines, which belong to the sauropod superfamily Diplodocoidea.
facts.quote: Se encontraron unos 100 fragmentos, la mayoría las espinas neurales, permitiendo a los investigadores de la UFRJ, Ismar de Souza Carvalho, Leonardo dos Santos Avilla, y el argentino Leonardo Salgado, identificar las nuevas especies que pertenecen a la superfamilia de saurópodos llamada Diplodocoidea.

facts.statement: The genus and species were named in 2003 by Brazilian paleontologists Ismar de Souza Carvalho, Leonardo dos Santos Avilla, and their Argentine colleague Leonardo Salgado.
facts.quote: El género y las especies fueron nombrados en 2003 por los paleontólogos brasileños Ismar de Souza Carvalho y Leonardo dos Santos Avilla, y su colega de Argentina, Leonardo Salgado.

facts.statement: The generic name is derived from the Brazilian Amazon region and the Greek word sauros, meaning 'lizard'.
facts.quote: El nombre genérico se deriva de la región amazónica brasileña y el término griego; sauros (" lagarto").

facts.statement: The single named species, A. maranhensis, is named after the Brazilian state of Maranhão.
facts.quote: Hay una especie nombrada, A. maranhensis (se pronuncia marañensis en portugués), de las cuales se debe al estado brasileño de Maranhão.

facts.statement: Although other dinosaurs have been found in inland Brazil, this is the first genus named from the Amazon Basin territory.
facts.quote: A pesar de que otros dinosaurios se han encontrado en el interior de Brasil, éste es el primer género nombrado del territorio de la Cuenca del Amazonas.

facts.statement: The geological formation dates to the Aptian and Albian stages of the Early Cretaceous, approximately 125 to 100 million years ago.
facts.quote: Esta formación geológica data de Aptiense y Albiense del Cretácico inferior, hace alrededor de 125 a 100 millones de años.

facts.statement: Amazonsaurus is the only dinosaur identifiable at the generic level from the Itapecuru Formation in Maranhão.
facts.quote: Los fósiles de Amazonsaurus, incluyen y vértebras de la cola y lomo, costillas, y los fragmentos de la pelvis, es el único dinosaurio identificable a nivel genérico de la Formación Itapecuru de Maranhão.

facts.statement: The fossils were recovered from sediments interpreted by geologists as alluvial terrain deposited near a river delta.
facts.quote: Esta formación geológica data de Aptiense y Albiense del Cretácico inferior, hace alrededor de 125 a 100 millones de años. Amazonsaurus fue recuperado en sedimentos que fueron interpretados por los geólogos como terreno aluvional que se depositó cerca de un delta de río.

facts.statement: High dorsal spines on the tail vertebrae identify Amazonsaurus as a diplodocoid sauropod, though the fragmentary nature of the single specimen makes specific placement difficult.
facts.quote: Las altas espinas dorsales de las vértebras de la cola identifican a Amazonsaurus como un saurópodo diplodocoide, pero la naturaleza fragmentaria del único espécimen conocido hace difícil colocar A. maranhensis más específicamente dentro de la superfamilia Diplodocoidea.

facts.statement: Some characteristics of the vertebrae suggest it may be a late-surviving member of a basal diplodocoid lineage.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, algunas características de estas vértebras sugieren que pueda ser un miembro tardío superviviente de una línea basal de diplodocoides.

facts.statement: At least one published cladistic analysis shows Amazonsaurus as more derived than rebbachisaurids but more basal than dicraeosaurids and diplodocids within Diplodocoidea.
facts.quote: Por lo menos un análisis cladístico publicado muestra a Amazonsaurus como un individuo más derivado que los rebaquisáuridos, pero más basal que los dicreosáuridos y diplodócidos dentro de Diplodocoidea.

facts.statement: The parent group for Amazonsaurus is Rebbachisauridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Rebbachisauridae

facts.statement: Amazonsaurus belongs to the family Rebbachisauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Rebbachisauridae

facts.statement: Amazonsaurus is classified in the class Saurischia.
facts.quote: Class: Saurischia

facts.statement: The time range for Amazonsaurus is from the Aptian to the Albian, between 119.57 and 106.3 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Albian (119.57 to 106.3 million years ago)

facts.statement: Researchers speculate that Amazonsaurus could swim due to its lower weight, which would be advantageous for defending against predators or navigating the environment.
facts.quote: Los investigadores también especulan que Amazonasaurus podía nadar debido a su menor peso, con una característica ventajosa para que pueda defenderse de los depredadores o llegar en un entorno como este.

facts.statement: Fossils of reptiles, terrestrial mollusks, pollen, and fish found at the site indicate the area was a plain constantly flooded by perennial rivers and streams with abundant fauna and flora.
facts.quote: En el lugar del hallazgo también se encontraron restos de reptiles, moluscos terrestres de polen y de peces fósiles, lo que indica que la zona habitada por Amazonasaurus era una llanura que constantemente inundado de ríos y arroyos perennes y abundante fauna y flora.
